# Leaderboard: Game-Over Score Entry and localStorage Display

## Problem Statement

The game currently has no scoring system, no game-over screen, and no leaderboard. When the player runs out of lives, the game respawns infinitely with no termination. The player has no way to record or view their high scores.

## Users

- **Player**: Completes the game (or dies) and wants to record their score by entering 3-character initials. They want to see their scores ranked against previous attempts on the game-over screen and from the main menu.

### User Stories

- As a player, when I run out of lives, I want to see my final score and be prompted to enter my initials so I can record my achievement.
- As a player, after entering my initials, I want to see the full leaderboard ranked by score so I can see how I compare to my past scores.
- As a player, from the main menu, I want to view the leaderboard to see my best scores.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Score tracking**: Each enemy type has a defined `scoreValue`. When an enemy is destroyed, its `scoreValue` is added to the player's total score. The score is displayed in the HUD (top-right corner, neon-styled numeric display).

2. **Game-over condition**: When the player's lives reach 0 (starting at 3, max 5 via P8 Extra Life), the game stops respawning and transitions to the game-over screen. There is no continue mechanic. The game-over screen shows the final score, an option to save (if score qualifies), and a restart button.

3. **Initials entry**: On the game-over screen, the player is prompted to enter exactly 3 uppercase letters (A-Z) as initials. Input is validated (only A-Z accepted, exactly 3 characters). [ASSUMPTION: on-screen clickable keyboard styled to match the neon terminal aesthetic.]

4. **localStorage persistence**: Entries are stored in browser localStorage under the key `ai_hell_leaderboard`. The stored data is a JSON array of entry objects (max 10 entries). When a new score qualifies for the leaderboard (i.e., would rank within the top 10), the player can enter initials to save it. If the score does not qualify, the player is informed and may skip the entry.

5. **Leaderboard display**: The game-over screen displays the full leaderboard showing rank, initials, score, and date for each entry, sorted by score (highest first). The leaderboard is also accessible from the main menu.

## Constraints

- Browser `localStorage` only (no backend, per GDD §5.1 — "single-machine" MVP).
- Maximum 10 leaderboard entries.
- Initials must be exactly 3 characters, uppercase letters only.
- Date format: ISO YYYY-MM-DD (per GDD data model example).
- The leaderboard data structure must support future abstraction for online leaderboards (GDD §5.3 migration note).

## Existing State

- **No score tracking exists**: No `scoreValue` on enemies, no score counter, no score display.
- **No game-over condition**: The `GymFormationScene` has infinite respawn — when all enemies are wiped, the formation respawns regardless of player lives.
- **Lives tracking exists**: `EffectsRegistry` tracks lives (starts at 3, caps at 5), displayed via the HUD. But lives are never decremented on player death.
- **No main menu**: The only entry scene is `GymIndex` (dev-mode gym scene launcher). No `MainMenuScene` exists.
- **No leaderboard code**: No localStorage operations for leaderboard, no initials input, no game-over screen.
- **GDD references**: `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts` are predicted but not yet implemented.

## Desired Change

1. **`src/core/Leaderboard.ts`** — Leaderboard persistence module:
   - `getEntries()`: Read and parse entries from localStorage.
   - `addEntry(initials: string, score: number)`: Add a new entry, maintain max 10, sort by score.
   - `getTopN(n: number)`: Return top N entries.
   - `isQualifying(score: number)`: Check if score would make the top 10.
   - Data structure: `{ rank, initials, score, date }` per GDD §5.2.

2. **Score tracking in `GymFormationScene`**:
   - Assign `scoreValue` to each enemy type (Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50 per, Boss: 1000 — [ASSUMPTION values, to be confirmed]).
   - Track player score as a counter in the scene.
   - Add score to total on enemy destroy.
   - Display score in the HUD (top-right).

3. **Game-over screen (`src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts`)**:
   - Displays final score, player initials input, and leaderboard.
   - Neon-styled UI matching the game aesthetic.
   - On-screen 3x3 grid keyboard for initials entry.
   - "Submit" button validates and saves the entry.
   - "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex for now).

4. **Main menu (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`)**:
   - "Play" button to start the game.
   - "Leaderboard" button to view the full leaderboard.
   - "Gym" button to access the gym index.
   - [NOTE: Main menu creation scope — see open questions.]

5. **Lives integration**:
   - Decrement lives on player hit (when invulnerable period ends).
   - When lives reach 0, transition to game-over screen.
   - Stop the respawn loop when game-over is triggered.

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope risk — main menu creation**: Creating a full main menu scene is a significant addition. If scope is constrained, the leaderboard may be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead, with the main menu deferred to a separate work item.
- **Scope risk — score tracking from scratch**: No score infrastructure exists. Implementing scoreValue on all enemy types, the score counter, and HUD display adds non-trivial work to GymFormationScene.
- **Assumption — enemy score values**: The GDD defines `scoreValue` on enemies but does not specify numeric values. The values in the draft are estimates and should be tuned.
- **Assumption — keyboard UI**: On-screen clickable keyboard was assumed; a producer decision is needed on input mechanism.
- **Assumption — game-over restart flow**: "Restart" returns to main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu). No "Play Again" shortcut from game-over.
- **Scope guard**: Level progression, boss mechanics, difficulty scaling, online leaderboards, and persistent game state between sessions are out of scope.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/core/Leaderboard.ts` — New file: leaderboard localStorage persistence
- `src/scenes/GameOverScene.ts` — New file: game-over screen with initials input and leaderboard display
- `src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts` — New file: main menu with leaderboard access [scope TBD]
- `src/scenes/gym/core/GymFormationScene.ts` — Modify: add score tracking, game-over condition, lives decrement
- `src/ui/HUD.ts` — Modify: add score display (top-right)
- `src/entities/BaseEnemy.ts` / `src/entities/*.ts` — Modify: add `scoreValue` to enemy types
- `src/core/Game.ts` — Modify: register new scenes, update boot flow
- `src/core/gameConfig.ts` — Modify: add MainMenu/GameOver to scene list for shipped build

## Related Work

- **AH-0MTZWZ1MQ004L552**: Create a playable game (parent epic, high priority, in `idea` stage) — includes main menu and playable game scope. This work item is a child of this epic.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **AH-0MU6VSKZT006HBTR**: Leaderboard — discovered-from the playable-game epic; the GDD (§5) is the authoritative spec.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.
- **GDD §6.4**: Technical architecture — predicted `src/core/GameState.ts` and `src/scenes/Menu.ts`.
- **AH-0MU3VOQKH005YOBH**: Combat gym scenes (gym scenes where power-up layer is shared) — uses the same `GymFormationScene` base.
- **AH-0MT985VRY009JXLZ**: Gym index scene (completed) — current entry point.
- **GDD §5**: Leaderboard design document — authoritative spec.
- **GDD §4.5**: Game-over conditions — 3 lives, no continue, score submission.

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

- **Q1**: Main menu scope — Should this work item include creating the Main Menu scene (`src/scenes/MainMenuScene.ts`), or should that be a separate work item? The GDD references `src/ui/Menu.ts` ("Main menu, game-over screen") but it has not been implemented. The leaderboard must be "accessible from the main menu" per the work item description. **Assumption**: This work item creates the main menu scene with leaderboard access. If the producer disagrees, the main menu creation should be a separate work item, and the leaderboard should be accessible from the existing GymIndex instead (or from the game-over screen itself).

- **Q2**: Score tracking scope — Should this work item include implementing score tracking from scratch (enemy `scoreValue` assignment, score counter, HUD display, points on destroy), or should score tracking be a prerequisite completed by a separate work item? **Assumption**: Score tracking is included in scope — it is fundamental to the leaderboard feature.

- **Q3**: Initials input mechanism — How should the 3-character initials entry work? Options: (a) on-screen clickable keyboard (A-Z grid, neon-styled), (b) browser-native text input styled with CSS, (c) other mechanism. **Assumption**: On-screen clickable keyboard matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q4**: Enemy `scoreValue` values — What point values should each enemy type carry? Scout, Diver, Tank, Phaser, Swarm (per-unit), Boss? **Assumption**: Scout: 100, Diver: 150, Tank: 200, Phaser: 300, Swarm: 50, Boss: 1000. These can be tuned later via the game-rules config.

- **Q5**: Score format — Should the score display show formatted numbers (e.g., "50,000") or raw (e.g., "50000")? **Assumption**: Raw numeric display (no commas) matching the neon terminal aesthetic.

- **Q6**: Game-over flow — After submitting a score (or declining to submit), should the game-over screen offer a "Restart" button that returns to the main menu, or should it auto-restart? **Assumption**: "Restart" button returns to the main menu (or GymIndex if no main menu exists). "Play Again" is not available until a score is submitted or declined.

# Intake Brief: Restore gym-game parity — wire missing power-up behaviours into PlayScene

## Problem statement

The playable game (PlayScene) diverged from the gym scenes: several power-up behaviours (magnet pull, speed boost, teleport, shield/phase visuals, per-type audio) are implemented and tested only in gym scenes but not wired into PlayScene. As a result, collecting power-ups P3/P4/P5/P6/P7/P8/P9/P5 in the game produces no visible or audible effect, violating GDD §4.4 and §7.3 requirements.

## Users (example user stories)

- As a player, I want visual and audio feedback for every power-up I collect, so I can perceive the effects the game is applying.
- As a tester, I want the game and gym scenes to exercise the same production code paths, so parity is measurable and bugs are caught earlier.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1** — In PlayScene, when magnetStacks() > 0, each collectible drop within the magnet radius is moved toward the player each tick at MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED (reuse the radius helper from powerups/effects.ts), with drop graphics position synced to the new logical x/y (visual pull animation).
- **AC2** — PlayScene applies the registry speed multiplier to the player ship each tick via setSpeedMultiplier(effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()), so P5 visibly boosts movement for its 10 s duration; multiplier re-applied every frame and returns to 1 after expiry.
- **AC3** — PlayScene binds S and ↓ as teleport-activation keys (JustDown semantics): pressing with at least one stored P7 stack warps the player to the nearest safe spot in the direction of travel via findTeleportDestination (enemy + bullet avoidance, screen-clamped), consuming one stack FIFO and granting P6 Phase Shift; with zero stacks nothing happens.
- **AC4** — PlayScene renders a visible shield bubble around the ship (lineStyle + low-alpha fill circle, radius SHIP_SIZE*1.6) while P3 is active (mirror GymPowerUpsCombat visuals), and when the shield absorbs a hit the bubble disappears and the player gets the brief invulnerability blink.
- **AC5** — PlayScene renders the ship as a semi-transparent ghost (alpha ~0.45) while P6 Phase Shift is active (mirror GymPowerUpsCombat), with ghost alpha deferring to the post-hit invulnerability blink when that is active, and full alpha restored on expiry.
- **AC6** — PlayScene shows a short centred 'BOMB! Bullets cleared' notice (mirroring GymPowerUpsCombat _flashBombNotice, label or HUD flash of similar prominence) on P4 collection; P4 continues to clear all on-screen enemy bullets and does not damage enemies.
- **AC7** — PlayScene plays the per-weapon fire cue for each weapon that fired in a volley (one cue per weapon, not per bullet) in _autoFire, mirroring GymWeapons _playShootCue; cues are safe no-ops without an AudioContext.
- **AC8** — PlayScene plays the appropriate per-type activation cue on collect for each distinct type (P3 shield, P4 bomb, P5 speed, P6 phase, P7 teleport, P8 extra life, P9 magnet, and weapon drops: spread/dual/rapid/reset) using the existing audio functions, with generic chime fallback where no dedicated cue exists.
- **AC9** — PlayScene plays each enemy's specific destruction audio where the entity exposes playDestructionAudio() (e.g. Diver → playDiverDestructionSound, Boss → playBossDestructionSound), falling back to the generic playDestructionSound otherwise, with no double-play on player-body-vs-enemy collision.
- **AC10** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints

- Prefer shared/module-level implementations so gyms and game exercise the same production code (per RCA root cause).
- Do not change power-up duration, radius, attraction speed, multiplier, or GDD §4.4 semantics.
- Audio cues must be safe no-ops without an AudioContext.
- The shared combat gym base (GymFormationScene) may also need wiring for magnet pull and speed multiplier to maintain gym parity.
- All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Existing state

| Deviation | Gym implementation | PlayScene state |
|-----------|-------------------|-----------------|
| P9 Magnet pull | GymPowerUps._applyMagnet — moves drops toward ship | No attraction logic in _updateDrops |
| P5 Speed Boost | GymPowerUps tick() calls setSpeedMultiplier | Never called in PlayScene |
| P7 Teleport | GymPowerUpsCombat + GymFormationScene — S/↓ → findTeleportDestination | No handling; stacks accumulate but unused |
| P3 Shield visual | GymPowerUpsCombat draws bubble | tryAbsorbShield works, no bubble or blink |
| P6 Phase visual | GymPowerUpsCombat sets alpha 0.45 | Collision skip works, no alpha change |
| P4 Bomb notice | GymPowerUpsCombat flashes 'BOMB!' label | Bullets cleared, no notice |
| Weapon fire audio | GymWeapons._playShootCue | _autoFire plays nothing |
| Pickup audio | GymPowerUps/GymWeapons play per-type cues | Only generic chime |
| Enemy destruction audio | GymFormationScene prefers playDestructionAudio | Always generic playDestructionSound |

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — Core scene logic; needs magnet, speed, teleport, visuals, audio wiring
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUps.ts` — Reference implementation for magnet, speed, pickup audio
- `src/scenes/gym/GymPowerUpsCombat.ts` — Reference for shield bubble, phase ghost, bomb notice
- `src/scenes/gym/GymFormationScene.ts` — Reference for teleport, enemy destruction audio
- `src/powerups/effects.ts` — EffectsRegistry; magnetStacks, speedMultiplier, consumeTeleport already exist
- `src/powerups/teleport.ts` — findTeleportDestination shared helper; already exists
- `src/entities/Player.ts` — setSpeedMultiplier, physicsTick; already supports multiplier
- `src/audio/effects.ts` — Per-type audio functions; already exist but unused in PlayScene
- `src/scenes/gym/GymWeapons.ts` — Reference for per-weapon fire cue dispatch
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — New/updated tests for each deviation

## Related work

- **AH-0MU72SZP1005X14G** — Create core game scene infrastructure (completed)
- **AH-0MU7305Z2003NII3** — Implement PlayScene — wave management integration (completed)
- **AH-0MU730M3T008C7CQ** — Integrate boss encounter into PlayScene (completed)
- **AH-0MU731IIZ001SQLA** — Implement scene navigation (completed)
- **AH-0MU8BZ2ZM004J47F** — Asteroids as an enemy (parent of PlayScene Integration + Unit Tests)
- **AH-0MU8FORFF005RD9M** — PlayScene Integration + Unit Tests (open, separate scope)
- **AH-0MU7JTFM5000R4ME** — Power-ups spawn too close together (completed)
- **AH-0MU7JTF9W008B8HW** — Player cannot move during transitions (completed)
- **AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG** — Root cause analysis that led to this epic
- **AH-0MU731VTE004PPC9** — Integrate HUD during gameplay (completed)
- **AH-0MU732AJW005RTG1** — Write tests for new game scenes and systems (completed)
- **AH-0MTZWZ1MQ004L552** — Create a playable game (completed)

## Risks & Assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** Extracting shared helpers for magnet pull and speed boost may uncover additional gym-specific logic that needs extraction — scope should remain focused on wiring existing gym logic into PlayScene, not refactoring gym scenes beyond what's necessary for shared code.
- **Assumption:** EffectsRegistry methods (magnetStacks, speedMultiplier, consumeTeleport, etc.) are already fully functional in PlayScene — the issue is only that PlayScene doesn't consume them. Verified via child descriptions.
- **Risk:** The teleport safe-spot resolver (findTeleportDestination) assumes an enemy list is available in PlayScene's tick context — must verify the enemy list is accessible from the same code path as teleport activation.
- **Risk:** Audio cue integration in PlayScene may require exposing the audio module's test seams for unit testing — must ensure the existing audio mock/stub pattern supports this.
- **Risk:** The P3 shield bubble visual needs to be rendered at the correct depth (above gameplay, below HUD) — must verify the existing render layer system supports this in PlayScene.
- **Assumption:** Each child work item is independent — no inter-dependencies between deviations (e.g., teleport granting P6 doesn't need shield visual to be wired first). Confirmed via dependency edges.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No questions asked — the children already contain sufficient detail (user stories, acceptance criteria, existing state, constraints). The intake auto-skipped the interview because the seed context from the RCA and child work items was already comprehensive.

Gym=>game deviation 1 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). The magnet power-up (P9) does nothing in the playable game: drops are never pulled toward the ship.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect a Magnet (P9) during a run, all on-screen power-up drops should visibly slide toward my ship so the effect is observable (matching the GymPowerUps gym, AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG).

## Existing state
- GymPowerUps.ts implements the _applyMagnet logic: each collectible drop within the magnet radius (2x ship size + 50% per stack) moves toward the ship at MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED, with the drop graphics position synced to the logical position each frame (visual sync, commit 81624e8).
- PlayScene _updateDrops (src/scenes/PlayScene.ts) advances lifecycles and collection only — no magnet attraction at all.
- EffectsRegistry.magnetStacks() accumulates correctly in PlayScene (collect via applyCollect('P9')); nothing consumes it.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — In PlayScene, when magnetStacks() > 0, each collectible drop within the magnet radius is moved toward the player each tick step at MAGNET_ATTRACTION_SPEED (reuse the radius helper from powerups/effects.ts and constants).
- **AC2** — The drop graphics position is updated to its new logical x/y each frame (visual pull animation, as in AH-0MTV6NZ6A000GPVG).
- **AC3** — Prefer a shared, module-level magnet-attraction helper used by BOTH GymPowerUps/combat gyms and PlayScene, so gyms and game exercise the same production code (per RCA root cause). Refactoring GymPowerUps to call it is acceptable; behaviour must not regress.
- **AC4** — Unit tests: magnet pull moves a drop toward the ship; drop beyond radius is not pulled; overlapping drop is collected; stacked radius grows with stacks.
- **AC5** — All existing tests (incl. gym magnet tests) continue to pass; full suite green.

## Constraints
- Do not change magnet math, radius, attraction speed, or GDD §4.4 semantics (permanent, cap 5 stacks).
- The shared combat gym base (GymFormationScene) also lacks magnet pull — if the shared helper is added, wire it there too so gyms remain parity references.

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 2 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). Collecting P5 Speed Boost during a run does nothing: the ship speed never changes.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect a Speed Boost (P5) I expect +50% thrust/max-speed for 10 s (GDD §4.4), exactly as demonstrated in the GymPowerUps gym.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUps.ts tick() calls player.setSpeedMultiplier(effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier()) every frame, so P5 boosts movement live.
- PlayScene tick() drives input/physics (player.physicsTick) but NEVER applies the speed multiplier — setSpeedMultiplier is not called anywhere in PlayScene.
- EffectsRegistry.speedMultiplier() returns 1.5 while P5 is active; the Player supports live multiplier application.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene applies the registry speed multiplier to the player ship each tick (setSpeedMultiplier(effectsRegistry.speedMultiplier())), so P5 visibly boosts movement for its 10 s duration.
- **AC2** — The multiplier is re-applied every frame (P5 is timed — must return to 1 after expiry) and survives respawns during an active P5.
- **AC3** — Prefer applying the same integration the gym uses; if a shared helper exists/extracted, gym and game both use it.
- **AC4** — Unit tests: P5 active → speedMultiplier applied (movement config scaled); P5 expired → multiplier back to 1; re-collect refreshes duration.
- **AC5** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change P5 duration, multiplier, or registry semantics.
- Note: the shared combat gym base (GymFormationScene) also never applies the speed multiplier — if addressed via shared code, wire it there too so gyms remain parity references.

Gym=>game deviation 3 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). The P7 Teleport power-up does nothing in the playable game: there is no S/↓ handling, no safe-spot resolution, and collected teleport stacks can never be consumed.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when I collect a Teleport (P7) and press S or ↓, I expect to warp to the nearest safe spot in the direction of travel (free of enemies and bullets, clamped to screen bounds), consuming one stored stack, and gain P6 Phase Shift on arrival (GDD §4.4) — exactly as in the combat gyms.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUpsCombat.ts and GymFormationScene.ts both implement _handleTeleport (S/↓ JustDown), triggerTeleport, findTeleportDestination (safe-spot resolver in powerups/teleport.ts), effectsRegistry.consumeTeleport() (FIFO stack + P6 via applyPhaseShift), movement-state sync, and a position update.
- PlayScene has NO teleport handling: no S/↓ key binding beyond WASD movement, no triggerTeleport, no safe-spot call. _collectDrop calls applyCollect('P7') so stacks accumulate in the registry but can never be used.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene binds S and ↓ as teleport-activation keys (JustDown semantics, so movement still works — S is also move-down in the 4-directional scheme, matching the gyms).
- **AC2** — Pressing S/↓ with at least one stored P7 stack warps the player to the nearest safe spot in the direction of travel via findTeleportDestination (enemy + bullet avoidance, screen-clamped), consuming one stack FIFO and granting P6 Phase Shift.
- **AC3** — Pressing S/↓ with zero stacks does nothing; no auto-repeat teleports.
- **AC4** — Player movement state (velocity/position used by physicsTick) is kept in sync after the warp, mirroring the gym implementation.
- **AC5** — Unit tests cover: teleport with stacks (warps, consumes, P6 granted), no stacks (no-op), destination respects enemy/bullet safety, and S/↓ input handling.
- **AC6** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Reuse the shared findTeleportDestination + registry consumeTeleport — do not duplicate resolution logic in PlayScene.
- Teleport activation is S or ↓ per GDD §2.1/§2.3 (already changed from Space in AH-0MTV7KAGZ006ER8R).
data.title: PlayScene: wire P7 Teleport (S/↓) with safe-spot resolution

data.description:
Gym=>game deviation 4 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). P3 Shield absorbs hits in PlayScene, but there is no shield bubble visual and no post-absorb invulnerability blink.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, when my shield (P3) is active I want to SEE the shield bubble around my ship, and when a hit is absorbed I expect the bubble to pop and a brief invulnerability blink, matching the GymPowerUpsCombat gym.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUpsCombat.ts _updateVisuals draws a shield bubble (lineStyle + low-alpha fill circle radius SHIP_SIZE*1.6) around the ship while effectsRegistry.isShielded, and _handleHits pops the shield (tryAbsorbShield) then _startInvulnerability() for a short blink.
- PlayScene _hitPlayer() calls effectsRegistry.tryAbsorbShield() — the hit is correctly absorbed (no life lost, AC of the combat gym) — but no bubble is rendered and no blink runs after absorb.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene renders a visible shield bubble around the ship while P3 is active (mirror the GymPowerUpsCombat visuals; depth above gameplay).
- **AC2** — When the shield absorbs a hit, the bubble disappears and the player gets the brief invulnerability blink (same as gym hit-response), so the absorb is observable.
- **AC3** — Prefer a shared visual helper if one is extracted, so gym and game render the bubble identically (scope: extraction optional; duplication acceptable if kept minimal per RCA constraints).
- **AC4** — Unit tests: bubble visible while shielded; after absorb bubble gone + invulnerable window started + life NOT lost.
- **AC5** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change shield duration (15 s), absorb semantics, or GDD §4.4 behaviour.

Gym=>game deviation 8 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). Power-up collection in PlayScene always plays the generic pickup chime — no per-type activation cues.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, I want a unique, recognisable activation cue for each power-up I collect (additional to the generic chime or replacing it), so I know at a glance which bonus I got — per GDD §7.3 'Pickup activation cues are unique per pickup type and distinct from the generic collection chime'.

## Existing state
- GymPowerUps.ts plays per-type cues on collect: playSpeedBoostCollectSound (P5), playExtraLifeCollectSound (P8), playMagnetCollectSound (P9).
- GymWeapons.ts plays per-type weapon pickup cues: playSpreadPickupSound/playDualPickupSound/playRapidPickupSound/playResetPickupSound.
- PlayScene _collectDrop always plays only playPowerUpCollectSound() regardless of type — P5/P8/P9/weapon drop activation cues (which exist in src/audio/effects.ts) are never played in the game.
- Note: GymPowerUpsCombat and GymFormationScene also use only the generic chime — the per-type cues exist only for the subset shown in those gyms. The game should match the GDD spec and the gyms that DO implement per-type cues.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene plays the appropriate per-type activation cue on collect for each distinct type: P3 shield, P4 bomb, P5 speed, P6 phase, P7 teleport, P8 extra life, P9 magnet, and weapon drops (spread/dual/rapid/reset) — matching the GDD §7.3 palette and reusing the existing audio functions. Where no dedicated cue exists in the audio module for a type, use the generic chime (documented gap, create a separate audio work item if a new cue is needed).
- **AC2** — Behaviour of collection (effects applied) is unchanged.
- **AC3** — Unit tests: collecting each type triggers its cue via the audio test seam; generic fallback for types without dedicated cues.
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change effect semantics or drop logic.
- Keep cues safe no-ops without AudioContext.

Gym=>game deviation 9 (parent AH-0MU8QTLYN003JV8M). Enemy destruction in PlayScene always plays the generic destruction sound; per-enemy destruction audio is ignored.

## Goal (user story)
As a player, I want enemies to sound distinct when destroyed (e.g. the Diver's unique destruction sound, Boss's destruction sound), matching the combat gyms and the per-enemy audio character in docs/ENEMY_DESIGN_AND_IMPLEMENTATION.md.

## Existing state
- GymFormationScene (shared combat gym base) prefers entity.playDestructionAudio() when the entity exposes the seam (Diver → playDiverDestructionSound, Boss → playBossDestructionSound via playDestructionAudio) and falls back to the generic playDestructionSound otherwise. It also avoids double-playing on player-body collision.
- PlayScene._handleCollisions always calls destroySelf() + playDestructionSound() for enemies (lines ~783, ~844), never calling playDestructionAudio — so Diver/Boss (and any future per-enemy audio) sound generic in the game.
- Entities already implement the playDestructionAudio seam (Diver.ts:291, Boss.ts:863); Tank has playTankDestructionSound in the audio module.

## Acceptance criteria
- **AC1** — PlayScene plays each enemy's specific destruction audio where the entity exposes playDestructionAudio() (e.g. Diver, Boss), falling back to the generic sound otherwise — matching the gym base behaviour.
- **AC2** — No double-play: on player-body-vs-enemy collision (step 4), the enemy destruction audio is played once (gym base plays entity audio there and lets _hitPlayer own the generic player-hit sound).
- **AC3** — Unit tests: bullet kill of a Diver plays the diver sound (via audio seam); a generic enemy plays the generic sound; collision path plays exactly once.
- **AC4** — Full test suite passes.

## Constraints
- Do not change enemy damage, scores, or kill logic.
- Prefer sharing the destruction-audio dispatch with the gym base if a helper can be extracted without behaviour change.

data.description:
# Asteroids should not explode when time runs out, instead carry them over

Asteroids persist through wave-timeout instead of detonating like other enemies, carrying over into the next wave at their current position and remaining shootable.

**Problem statement:** When the wave timer expires, all surviving enemies (including asteroids) detonate at 10x scale and cost the player a life. Asteroids are a special enemy type that should survive wave-timeout and carry over to the next wave, continuing their movement and remaining shootable — consistent with classic Asteroids gameplay where asteroids persist independently of wave timing.

**Users:** Players of the game who expect classic Asteroids behaviour where asteroids persist between waves.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

1. When the wave timer expires, asteroids (all size tiers) are excluded from the 10x-scale detonation — they remain alive at their current position and velocity.
2. Surviving asteroids continue their straight-line movement, screen-edge wrapping, and rotation into the next wave.
3. Surviving asteroids are shootable during the level start banner / transition period (before the next wave's enemies spawn).
4. All other (non-asteroid) enemies still explode at 10x scale, cost one life, and trigger normal wave advancement.
5. Automated tests verify asteroid survival on timeout, non-asteroid explosion still occurs, and surviving asteroids are shootable.

**Constraints:**

- Only asteroids (any size tier) are affected; all other enemy types retain current timeout behaviour.
- The existing life-loss penalty and wave advancement on timeout remain unchanged.
- Asteroids that survive should retain their current position, velocity, and rotation state.
- No changes to the Asteroid entity class itself — only the scene-level timeout logic changes.

**Existing state:** `PlayScene._timeoutWave()` iterates all surviving enemies in `this.spawned` and calls `destroySelf(WAVE_TIMEOUT_EXPLOSION_SCALE)` on each — including asteroids. This causes asteroids to explode and be removed.

**Desired change:** In `_timeoutWave()`, filter asteroids out of the explosion list. They survive and carry over. The scene's existing `update()` loop will continue to call `updatePosition()` on them, maintaining their movement.

**Key Files (predicted):**

- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — `_timeoutWave()` method needs to skip asteroids when detonating survivors
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.test.ts` — new test for asteroid survival on wave-timeout
- `src/entities/Asteroid.ts` — existing entity class (no changes needed)

**Risks & assumptions:**

- **Risk: scope creep** — Adding asteroid-specific timeout behaviour could accidentally interact with split children or other special enemies. Mitigation: the change is isolated to `_timeoutWave()` filtering logic; split spawns are unrelated.
- **Risk: position/velocity preservation** — Surviving asteroids must retain their exact position and velocity at timeout. Assumption: the existing `updatePosition()` call in the scene loop handles this automatically (no explicit state save needed).
- **Risk: test edge cases** — Need to verify that asteroid split children spawned after timeout behave normally. Assumption: standard split logic is unaffected since it runs via `onEnemyDestroyed`, not `_timeoutWave()`.
- **Scope-creep opportunity** — Other special enemy types (if any) might also need timeout exemption in future. Record as a future consideration, not in scope.

**Related work:**

- **AH-0MU7JTG9R002ZWA6** — Wave time limit: surviving enemies detonate at 10x scale and cost a life (the parent timeout mechanic that this bug fix specialises)
- **AH-0MU8FOQ7L005AII0** — Core Asteroid Entity + Unit Tests (the Asteroid entity class)
- **AH-0MU8FORFF005RD9M** — PlayScene Integration + Unit Tests (the scene where the fix applies)
data.title: Asteroids should not explode when time runs out, instead carry them over
